answer: A farm that floods the queue early therefore gains nothing from the flood while paying the fee on every entry. Because the cipher ordering is published with the nadir batch, the vertex audit can verify the shuffle and a biased queue would be visible. Submissions are shuffled by the beacon before review, so arriving first buys no advantage and only 43% of the queue is processed in arrival order. Honest users pay that once, farms 34 times. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
